result:
I've written the A06 API suite and the root e2e spec. The core A06 path works in English and Arabic. Two tests fail on purpose because they hit product defects, so the "all suites pass" acceptance check is not met. This was an authoring task, not a gate review; I wrote no review record and left everything uncommitted.

**Files:**
- `tests/qa/integration/a06-configuration-change.test.ts`: 27 API tests on their own scratch database, since they publish the shared Studio versions (forms, playbook, scoring defaults).
- `e2e/a06-configuration-change.spec.ts`: Playwright on the real stack, run in chromium-en and chromium-ar.
- `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/qa/T-DG5-QA-A-authoring/`: the handback, logs, screenshots and mutation logs.

**Checks (real exit codes):**

| Check | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| DG4 historical validation, at start and at end | 0 | PASS both times |
| All `tests/qa` integration suites | 1 | 16 files, 198 passed, 1 failed (A06 file: 26 passed, 1 failed; finding 1) |
| A06 e2e, `--workers=1` | 1 | Main test passed in both browsers, with 0 serious or critical axe issues on every checked screen; the T13 test failed in both (finding 2) |
| `pnpm lint` | 0 | clean |
| Prettier check over the repository | 0 | clean |

One deviation: Vitest can't load its config here because `node_modules` is read-only, so I ran it with `--configLoader runner`. This changes no test.

In the e2e, the admin uses the Studio UI to add a T01 field, change its maximum from 100 to 50, and change a gate's approver from Sponsor to Business Owner. With no restart, a new transformation stores 80. A newer one refuses 80 and stores 40. A record on the previous version keeps 80. The gate's exception goes to the Business Owner on a new transformation and to the Sponsor on an old one.

**Mutation checks:** I broke the product in a throwaway copy, never in this tree.
- **Caught:** five central assertions fail when their behaviour breaks: the field maximum, the 100% weights rule, deleting a TOM dimension, sequential routing, and blocking an admin as approver.
- **Survived:** three single-layer breaks survived because a database guard enforces the same rule with the same error. Breaking both layers made the tests fail.

**Findings** (proposed IDs; you allocate the final ones):
- **F-DG5-QA-A-1 (Medium):** on a new transformation, the Gates screens still show Sponsor as G3's approver after it was changed to Business Owner. Submissions are correctly routed to the Business Owner, who decides; the Sponsor gets 403. The API returns `gate.approverRoleCode: "SP"` next to `currentSubmission.approverRoleCode: "BO"`. The failing test is kept.
- **F-DG5-QA-A-2 (Medium):** a field added to T13 in Studio can't be entered or seen on the stakeholder record in the UI. Among the templates, only T01 and T14 have the record form; T02–T13, T15 and T16 don't. The failing e2e test is kept, with screenshots.
- **F-DG5-QA-A-3 (Medium):** the Studio UI can't set up sequential or parallel approval routes; its editor takes a single approver role only. I found this by reading the source; there is no test for it yet.
- **F-DG5-QA-A-4 (Low):** when a value is over the field's maximum, the refusal shows a number-format hint instead of saying the limit.
- **Observations:**
  - The automation dry run needs the full internal event payload, which the API contract doesn't describe.
  - A forms migration lists a new required field only when the transformation already has records of that type.
  - The FE-B report of empty catalogues after a methodology publish no longer reproduces.

**Not covered here:** retrying a failed automation (A13), the formula-change impact (A07), running each seeded procedure end to end (A02), the renamed product in the shell header and next report header, the affected-records view, and the export samples (A15/A16). The handback has the full requirement-to-test table, which marks each row covered, partial or not covered.
